source.title: Sparse Autoencoder Insights on Voice Embeddings
source.authors: Dan Pluth; Yu Zhou; V. Gurbani

record.file_problem: Text is readable and appears to contain the full paper; figure contents are not included in the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: Applies sparse autoencoders to speaker embeddings from a telephony-adapted Titanet model, a new modality and model setting, and reports results on feature recovery, splitting, and steering.
record.gate_note: The paper reports SAE feature classification, splitting, and steering results. It does not measure overlap or orthogonality of directions, feature-capacity competition, or the geometry of features. The cited LLM studies' findings are not this paper's results. Titanet's reported EER is not a result on the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study trains TopK SAEs on Titanet speaker embeddings, a non-LLM convolutional audio model. It reports whether sparse, recoverable features exist (language, hold music) and how they split with dictionary size. That is a new-setting result on V4's 'SAE can recover sparse features in real models' and on V5's canonicity. V4 names LLMs, so its verdicts are scoped to this non-LLM setting.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that SAEs extract mono-semantic, steerable features (language, music) from Titanet speaker embeddings that are not evident in the raw embedding, with feature splitting as the latent space grows. They state the work supports four of Anthropic's listed SAE properties: monosemanticity, hidden interpretable features, steering, and splitting. Universality is left for future work.
record.recipe_differences: This is not a reproduction of the original toy-network superposition method. It trains TopK sparse autoencoders on speaker embeddings, uses logistic-regression probes for selected attributes, and evaluates feature steering with centroid similarities.
record.method_sensitivity: Feature-classification performance depends on SAE latent dimension and TopK. Spanish feature splitting occurs at different latent dimensions across TopK settings and plateaus around 300 elements; music performance drops for low TopK.
record.peer_reviewed: 2025 Conference on Artificial Intelligence x Multimedia (AIxMM)
record.problems: The paper states that only a few easily labeled attributes were examined, that many latent features were not obvious from listening, and that the largest SAE latent space was only approximately 3x the input size. It reports no uncertainty estimates or control comparisons. Audio is private, and detailed per-configuration figure values are not available in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: Detailed per-configuration plotted values from Figures 2 and 3, and distribution values from Figures 5 and 6, are not recoverable from the supplied text. The text's aggregate descriptions and the numerical means in Tables III and IV are recorded.

untested.parts: All of it: no toy networks, no overlap or orthogonality measurements, no sparsity transition, no geometry.
All of it: no neuron-level polysemanticity or capacity analysis of the 192 embedding dimensions.

The LLM setting. Whether the raw embedding dimensions are polysemantic or spread features: no comparison of raw dimensions with SAE latents is reported. Dictionaries with many more latents than inputs (largest is ~3x).
Completeness, stability across seeds or runs, and universality across models (named by the authors as future work).
All of it. The authors say it is unclear how continuous features such as pitch are encoded.

missing.what: No English latent was found in any SAE. The authors read English as encoded as the default and say dictionaries reflect the SAE training data distribution, which bears on dictionary features being canonical units.
Error analysis: 91.0% of Spanish-latent false positives were native Spanish speakers speaking English. This suggests the latent tracks accent or speaker origin, not language strictly.

record.verdict_notes: The record's 'tests' relation is kept as T3, since V4 names LLMs but the study examines a convolutional audio model. There is no raw-dimension baseline, so the claim that features are 'not evident in the original embedding' is asserted, not measured. The headline numbers come from one chosen configuration (K=20, L=200), while most configurations show ~70% recall. No uncertainty estimates, seeds or controls are reported. The largest dictionary is only ~3x the input size.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, sparse features exceeding dimensions, overlapping nearly orthogonal directions, sparsity-dependent transition, and regular geometry.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise from capacity competition, or whether important features get dedicated dimensions while others share.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise for reasons other than capacity pressure.
The study tests SAE feature recovery in speaker embeddings, not in LLMs; it does not establish that real models generally spread features across many neurons.
It does not establish SAE feature completeness, stability across training runs or methods, or canonical status as the model's units.
The paper does not compare one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional features or measure their geometry.

relationships.condition: Non-LLM Titanet speaker embeddings, SAE K=20, latent 200, language and hold-music features
relationships.reason: Single SAE latents predict Spanish (P 99.2%/R 95.5%) and music (P 92.3%/R 99.1%) on held-out speakers. Toggling the latents flips the sign of centroid similarity (r1, r2, r9, r10, r12-r15).
relationships.display_finding: Single latents predicted Spanish (precision 99.2%, recall 95.5%) and music (precision 92.3%, recall 99.1%) on held-out speakers, and toggling them flipped the sign of centroid similarity.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Across the SAE grid (latent dim 100-1200, K 5-35)
source_check.reason: The reported configurations recover sparse features. Approximately 70% single-latent Spanish recall reflects splitting, and reduced music performance at low K does not establish absence of recoverable features. V4 requires neither configuration-invariant units nor uniformly high single-latent recall. Larger undertrained dictionary sizes were omitted from results.

relationships.condition: Spanish feature across dictionary sizes and TopK
relationships.reason: Spanish is a single latent at dims 100/200 but splits into male and female latents at 300. The split point varies with K, so the unit depends on SAE hyperparameters (r3, r5-r8).
relationships.display_finding: Spanish occupied a single latent at dictionary sizes 100 and 200 but split into male and female latents at 300, and the split point shifted with K.
